assessment_scope.source_boundary: Only the subject's two curated REVIEWED items at basis_commit, each read in full with its front matter: the active_provisional KONOSUBA_CHRIS_ERIS_CHARACTER_MONOGRAPH.md (17,054 bytes) and the active_provisional KONOSUBA_CHRIS_ERIS_RECONSTRUCTION_MODEL.md (24,777 bytes; seven informed rules CE-D-01 to CE-D-07 and six same-author source-known exercises). Both treat Chris and Eris as one continuing person across bodily roles. Their direct core is MAIN12 final chapter P1-438, MAIN17 C3 P200-402 and the Eris-focalized MAIN17 epilogue P1-93, plus CONTEXP01 U021 P1-80/P119-203/P329-375/P444-510 and U026 P1-50; the model says two of these five members have holes and that accepted MAIN01-12 and MAIN17 reports and early checkpoints are derivative context only, while the MAIN13-16 audit, later checkpoints, ledger consolidation and the identity and event census remain open. The evidence index, receiving and provenance manifests and the exercise inputs, outputs and causal review are not curated on this subject and were not used. The items' own reliability labels are inputs, not conclusions; the evaluator performed no primary-source inspection.
assessment_scope.temporal_boundary: Two located main-series states and one spin-off window: the MAIN12 final-chapter infiltration as familiar thief Chris, before Darkness learns her identity (the MAIN12 epilogue shows only that Darkness overheard that a secret exists); the MAIN17 C3 office state, in which Eris prepares Kazuma's return, and the MAIN17 epilogue, in which her premise changes within the scene from assumed death to his living Teleport; and the CONTEXP01 U021 and U026 windows, which the items do not place in the main chronology and which this record does not order against MAIN12-17. MAIN13-16 are open and are not covered. Knowledge states are time-indexed: later disclosure is never backdated, and her stated wish for Darkness to learn her identity is not a completed disclosure. Her own testimony that MAIN17 is her first voluntary rule-breaking is her account, not an audit of earlier interventions.
assessment_scope.assessment_method: characters/RECONSTRUCTION_CAPABILITY_SPEC.md and governance/policies/CHARACTER_RECONSTRUCTION_MAINTENANCE.md at basis_commit, including the owner calibration rulings; evidence-located calibration with countercases, explicit gaps and no model-readiness inheritance.

dimensions.note: The model requires representing bodily role and powers, knowledge and disclosure, the particular person, task and target, competing rewards and voice purpose before choosing a response, and gives seven rules with evidence, application conditions, expected response, rivals and counterevidence, limits, confidence and a falsifier. It predicts her mistakes as well as her help: accepting an untested generalization (the orc binding), defending a professional premise after contrary help, attacking on a demon identification against the agreed Bind, and inadequate wire-cutting recovery; it forbids granting her whichever tendency would make the outcome best. Where rivals recruit the same action (CE-D-01: concern, public obligation, pride or an impressive story), the predicted choice does not change, so the uncertainty is about attribution, not the decision. Not A: confidence is MODERATE for most transfer and LOW-MODERATE for CE-D-05, every rule is informed by already known sources, and the six exercises are same-author continuations. Not C: within-scene contrasts locate what changes her response (target information, a changed request premise, a gap exposed by offered help, a new admission).

The items keep MAIN12 Chris, MAIN17 office Eris and the CONTEXP01 windows separate and time-index knowledge (Darkness's overheard secret versus its content; the wish for future disclosure), but give no developmental account: MAIN13-16 are open, CONTEXP01 is not ordered against the main volumes, and change between states is not modeled. Not C: no state sequence with transitions is established. Not E: distinct located states and knowledge progressions are kept apart with paragraph locators.

Register is described functionally and conditioned: familiar Chris speech with ordinary first-person and assistant-address forms, repeated or pressing questions, playful hierarchy, sudden objections and flustered correction; public Eris speech with formal address and service framing; Eris inviting familiar speech while saying the form affects her register; a return to Chris's manner in MAIN17 C3 before any newly shown bodily change; and formal grammar delivering an unequivocal refusal (MAIN17 Ep P59). The items state that politeness is not consent and a question is not automatically care, and claim no heard timing, accent or performance. Not B: no pronoun, address or ending is named and no line is located for imitation; the exercises are English. Not D: the register shift is conditioned on role, audience and purpose with located occasions.

CE-D-04 gives a conditioned ordinary-company rule with a falsifier: an enthusiastic inn request, an appeal to shared adventure, acceptance of Darkness's payment, intrusive questions about friends' relationships and an incomplete answer about residence (MAIN12 F P6-24, P45-95), her own account of money going to the Eris church and drinking, and CONTEXP01 lunch, recruitment and performance work. Bounds are stated: the donation is her account, not an audited rule; withholding an address does not establish homelessness; shared company does not authorize access to every place. Not B: daily routine, residence and private life are not modeled, and the rule rests on a few scenes. Not D: the rule states conditions, an expected response, rivals and a falsifier.

The items distinguish Darkness (reciprocal material care, intrusive questions, concern about her standards, a wish for future disclosure; Darkness knows a secret exists, not its content), Kazuma (assistant and chief partnership, shared failures, rescue and teasing; he knows her identity yet can misread her reasons; a retracted counter-joke creates no romantic agreement), Aqua (seniority, respect and practical cooperation with competing judgments of risk and identity complications), Megumin (who knows the masked partnership but not the divine identity) and Cecily (guilt pressure and an unwanted performance). Each relation states what changes her response and where it stops, with knowledge kept participant-specific. Not A: the Aqua relation is thin and each relation rests on a few windows. Not C: the account is discriminating and bounded.

The MAIN17 epilogue is Eris-focalized, giving direct access to her thoughts there: an assumption that Kazuma died again, limited recent observation of the lower world, deliberate withholding of the castle bombing, sympathy retracted after his admission. Elsewhere interior states are inferred from conduct (crying after the orc capture, embarrassment, excitement, reluctance to harm a cute costume). The items state that her thoughts about others, such as Darkness's affection, remain her interpretations. Not B: direct interior access is confined to one ninety-three-paragraph epilogue. Not D: the focalized window and conduct-based states are located.

Three conflict mechanisms are located with within-scene contrasts, conditions and falsifiers: a newly identified demon displaces the agreed restraint with a lethal attack, and after correction she accepts a changed sequence while keeping the lethal end (CE-D-02, MAIN12 F P275-307); face protection delays acceptance of useful help without abolishing real skill (CE-D-03, P130-192); and an office intrusion she newly understands draws a firm refusal with a bounded alternative (CE-D-06, MAIN17 Ep P45-63). She also advocates a costly course to Kazuma over his objections (CE-D-01). Not A: each mechanism rests on one episode, and the exercise for CE-D-02 showed hostile preparation without the predicted attack. Not C: the conditions that switch her conduct are located.

Located value-laden choices with stated reasons: the office refusal grounded in dignity and jurisdiction; voluntary rule-breaking to prepare Kazuma, which she advocates with practical arguments, concern for people and stated attraction to the weakest boy defeating the king; concern about killing endangered male orcs beside lethal hostility toward a demon; sympathy retracted after a harem boast without loss of affection; a deliberate omission of known news. The items separate her justification from the target's actual conduct and the category's moral adequacy. Not B: an explicit weighing between options is reported in one exchange, and the demon category has no supplied ordinary-world equivalent. Not D: the choices and their stated grounds are located.

Located play: teasing and counter-joking with Kazuma, including an apparent marriage acceptance she retracts as attempted teasing (MAIN17 C3 P366-373); playful hierarchy and enjoyment of having an assistant, with her own instance exempted when she stops his enjoyment of being called senior (MAIN12 F P142-155); amusement at the group's coming trouble. Not C: no rule predicts when she teases rather than becomes flustered or protects face. Not E: several located exchanges with stated bounds.

Five direct members with paragraph locators, three complete at base-text scope and two with explicit holes; derivative context from accepted main reports; the MAIN13-16 audit, later checkpoints, ledger consolidation and identity and event census are declared open. Not C: the items say a useful model is earned at this boundary without a finished census, and a run of main volumes inside her span is unread for this subject. Not E: the declared core is located precisely and the items separate direct action, report, inference and proposal.

Affirmative adverse cases are retained as source facts: the rope-climbing failure, the wrong floor premise and the lifting-door mistake, the unsupported orc generalization and capture, guilt-based deflection, the information-triggered procedural breach, inadequate wire-cutting recovery, the human-role darkvision limit, her wrong assumption of Kazuma's death and limited observation, and the office refusal, which constrains any claim that affection produces service beyond her wishes. Further controls: Darkness's overheard secret is not its content; the retracted counter-joke is not an engagement; her donation account is not an audit; the CE-D-02 exercise showed no attack. Not A: some controls are analytic and the exercise evidence is same-author. Not C: the source-fact controls are specific and decisive.

Claims carry paragraph locators within named members, knowledge is time-indexed, and within-scene premise changes are located (MAIN17 Ep P45 versus P47-60). Not B: CONTEXP01 is not ordered against the main volumes, MAIN13-16 are open, and no cross-volume state conditions are given.

conditions: Translated illustrative lines only, never presented as quotation, in a sampled function: familiar Chris inquiry, teasing, boasting, objection or flustered correction with Darkness or Kazuma; public Eris service speech, information or preparation; or a polite but unequivocal refusal.
Choose register by role, audience and purpose; Eris may shift into familiar register without a shown bodily change; politeness never signals consent.
No pronoun, address or ending inventory, no catchphrase, stutter quota or apology rate, and no heard timing, accent or performance claims.
No line that reveals her divine identity to someone who lacks it, or treats the retracted marriage counter-joke as a settled preference.
scenario_readiness.note: The items constrain speech function, register shift and refusal enough for short illustrative lines in sampled situations, not Japanese forms, which they do not name.

conditions: Before predicting, fix her bodily role and available powers, what she knows and who else knows her identity, the particular person, the task and target, and the request's scope.

A known person's concrete need with an available contribution: she offers or attempts fitted help and may press a demanding plan; the recipient's agreement and the plan's adequacy are established separately (CE-D-01, moderate transfer).

A target newly identified as demonic during a restraint procedure, in canonical mode: hostility and fast attack are likely, and she may accept a sequence change while keeping the hostile end (CE-D-02, moderate-high within matched information states).

A friend's request that would change the function of her office or another protected workplace: refusal with a possible bounded alternative (CE-D-06); a one-day local extension under affiliation pressure from a sincere ally may draw reluctant compliance (CE-D-05, low-moderate). Abstain between these, and on cumulative public-service requests beyond her preferred load (the old CE01 test is untested).
Interlocutors are Darkness, Kazuma, Aqua, Megumin or Cecily; an unfamiliar petitioner or companion is a separate, lower-confidence case.

cross_scenario_scope.assumed_chronology: A located state: the MAIN12 final-chapter infiltration as familiar Chris before Darkness knows her identity, or the MAIN17 office state at or after Kazuma's living return; CONTEXP01 situations only as their own unordered windows; no MAIN13-16 state.
cross_scenario_scope.interlocutor_relationship: Darkness as a reciprocal friend who knows only that a secret exists, Kazuma as her assistant who knows her identity, Aqua as her senior, Megumin as someone who knows only the masked partnership, or Cecily as a pressing believer; anyone else only as a separate, lower-confidence case.
setting_constraints: Canonical mode: thief expeditions, the divine office, and the CONTEXP01 recruitment, performance and adventuring settings with source powers, bodily roles and jurisdiction preserved; a human-role Chris never uses an unestablished divine power and office Eris knows only what she observed, was told or was supplied.

Transfer mode may keep only enjoyable company, particular care, professional pride, selective disclosure, task-conflicting values and workplace boundaries, with powers specified as explicit resources; the demon category has no ordinary-world equivalent.
No anime adaptation, supplemental-only chronology or unread main-volume material.

scenario_readiness.note: Bounded extrapolation within the knowledge, request and target contrasts the rules sample; cumulative public service, MAIN13-16 states and ordinary-world analogues of the demon category are excluded.

conditions: Familiar company with Darkness or Kazuma (an inn, an outing, shared expenses, gossip): she may ask for company or support, accept a friend's payment, tease and press intrusive questions, warm and intrusive at once.
Her own money history is her account; withholding an address does not establish homelessness; no routine, home or private-life detail is invented.
Shared company never authorizes access to every place or disclosure; the office refusal remains a contrary condition.
scenario_readiness.note: CE-D-04 and the located ordinary scenes support bounded familiar-company situations, not daily routine or residence.

conditions: Requests that change the function of her office or jurisdiction: dignity and jurisdiction ground a refusal that preserves affection.
Whether to aid a particular person at real cost to them: she may advocate a demanding plan for practical, caring and aesthetic reasons, and the recipient's agreement is separate.
Demon targets only in canonical mode, with her hostility kept hers and never presented as well-calibrated punishment; no ordinary-world moral analogue.
scenario_readiness.note: Bounded to the value conflicts the items locate; her moral classification is portrayed, not endorsed.

The only romantic-coded exchange of her own is the MAIN17 marriage counter-joke she retracts as attempted teasing, which the items say establishes no engagement or hidden settled preference; her reading of Darkness's affection is an interpretation of another person.

conditions: Thief work: rope, stealth, enemy sensing and retrieval, with the located limits of arm strength, a wrong floor premise and treating a lifting door as a lock problem; face protection may delay acceptance of help (CE-D-03).
Divine office: Powered, Protection, Resist, Haste and Blessing as shown in MAIN17; her confidence in Blessing is her own domain claim, not supremacy in every spell.
No resource-free rescue, no unshown power in the human role, and no omniscient observation from the office.
scenario_readiness.note: Her strongest professional evidence is thief work and divine support magic, with located failures.

known_limits.statement: Whether cumulative public-service requests beyond her preferred load draw compliance or refusal is untested; the office refusal and the one-day Cecily recommitment do not score the old CE01 forecast, and the model rates affiliation-pressure compliance LOW-MODERATE.

In the same-author exercise for CE-D-02 the known-demon response drew a dagger and stated hostile intent but performed no strike, harm or procedural disruption, so it cannot validate the attack-and-displacement expectation; no exercise shows later boundary enforcement.

The person is continuous but powers are not: the human-role Chris has located limits of strength and sight, and divine office does not supply unlimited strength, knowledge, moral authority or availability.

Knowledge of her identity differs by participant: Kazuma knows it, Megumin knows only the masked partnership, Darkness knows only that a secret exists; reader-confirmed identity is never another character's knowledge.
The fictional demon category has no ordinary-world equivalent; transfer keeps only the conflict between rule, classification and objective.
The retracted marriage counter-joke establishes no engagement or settled preference.
Her money history is her own account, residence is withheld rather than absent, and no daily routine or private-life detail is established.
MAIN13-16, later checkpoints, ledger consolidation and the identity and event census are open; behavior in those volumes is unassessed and CONTEXP01 is not placed in the main chronology.
The evidence index, receiving and provenance manifests and the exercise inputs, outputs and causal review are not curated on this subject, so their contents were not read as evidence.
No pronoun, address or ending is named, and no Japanese fluency or performance test exists; the exercises are English continuations.
